overall_feedback: This is a careful and technically impressive experiment: two minimal Kitaev chains are coupled through a tunable quantum dot, single-shot parity readout is combined with nanosecond baseband pulses, and coherent oscillations between |ee> and |oo> (and, via a parity-switching dot, between |eo> and |oe>) are resolved with clear dependence on coupler detuning, superconducting phase and hybrid-gate settings. The effective-Hamiltonian analysis in Methods VIII-XI is mostly correct (I checked Eqs. (9)-(16), (20), (21) and (24)-(25)), and the authors are commendably explicit about the limits of what the effective model can say about spatial separation. My main concerns are about how strongly the data support the headline interpretation. (i) The even/odd frequency match is presented as evidence that both chains sit at the sweet spot with small Majorana overlap, yet matching frequencies and contrast in both manifolds is also the stated final criterion of the tuning procedure, the measured frequencies differ at roughly 6 sigma, and residual longitudinal splittings produce an even/odd frequency difference of the same second-order form as the overlap term attributed to epsilon_14. (ii) Several statements in the Methods contain sign or factor-of-two errors (the excited-state resonance condition, the sign of the residual splitting in Methods X, and the frequency formula above Eq. (22)). (iii) Using the authors' own noise parameters, the phi = pi analysis predicts dephasing within about 40 ns, which does not match the main-text statement that neither oscillations nor fast dephasing are seen there. (iv) The claims of a 'first coherent control of a Majorana qubit', 'close agreement' with the model, and a 'direct comparison' to a conventional charge qubit go further than what is shown: only Rabi-type rotations with Q of about 3 are demonstrated, the noise model is hand-tuned and qualitative, and the detuning range in Fig. 4g,h does not reach the double-dot limit. These points are fixable with corrected formulas, an explicit error budget and somewhat more careful wording, and the experiment itself remains a significant step for the quantum-dot Kitaev chain platform.

comments.title: Even/odd frequency agreement is partly built in by the tuning criterion
comments.quote: A successful tuning is indicated by oscillations with similar frequencies and contrast in both
comments.explanation: The main text presents the matching Rabi frequencies in the two global parity manifolds (Fig. 3b,h) as a test showing that both chains are at the sweet spot and that the inter-chain coupling is approximately parity independent, consistent with small Majorana overlap. Methods III, however, says that the final check of every tune-up is that Rabi oscillations in the even and odd manifolds have similar frequencies and contrast. If configurations are kept or rejected based on this condition, the agreement in Fig. 3b is partly a selection effect and cannot independently confirm the model. My first guess was that Fig. 3b might be taken over a range of VC where no retuning was done, which would make it a semi-independent test. But the figure only shows the dependence on VC at one tuning point, so the key question, whether the frequencies match at a tuning point chosen without looking at the frequencies, is not answered. There is also a second, physical degeneracy. Eq. (22) attributes the frequency difference entirely to epsilon_14. Residual longitudinal terms give f_even proportional to sqrt((eps12+eps34)^2 + eps23^2) and f_odd proportional to sqrt((eps12-eps34)^2 + eps23^2), so (f_odd - f_even)/(f_odd + f_even) is about -eps12*eps34/eps23^2. This is also a product of the two chains' deviations, of the same order as the mu_L1*mu_R2/(4 t_L t_R) term. A small measured difference therefore cannot be assigned to Majorana overlap rather than to residual mistuning of t - Delta in the two chains. Fig. 3d,e show that frequency rises with detuning, which supports this concern.
comments.suggested_fix: State explicitly which data sets were selected with the even/odd-matching criterion, and report the even/odd frequency comparison for tuning points fixed only by the pulsed charge-stability crossings (without the Rabi check). Generalize Eq. (22) to (f_even - f_odd)/(f_even + f_odd) ≈ eps14/eps23 + eps12*eps34/eps23^2, and state that the measured difference bounds the sum of both contributions, not epsilon_14 alone.

comments.title: Reported even and odd frequencies differ significantly, yet are called equal
comments.quote: (feven = 113.4 ± 0.5 MHz, fodd = 117.7 ± 0.4 MHz) in both parity manifolds
comments.explanation: The abstract says 'equal oscillation frequencies at the Majorana sweet spot' and the caption says 'nearly equal'. With the quoted fit uncertainties, the difference is 4.3 ± 0.64 MHz, about 6.7 standard deviations from zero. Methods VI states that the quoted uncertainties come from curve_fit with absolute_sigma=False and uniform point uncertainties, so they are purely statistical. The even and odd data are taken in separate sweeps, separated by retuning (Methods III: retuning before each 2D sweep, 1 to 4 hours per sweep), with separate pulse-amplitude calibrations in the two manifolds because of the QDPS-QDR2 charging energy. Systematic shifts between the two measurements are therefore likely to exceed the statistical error bars. As a result, it is not clear whether the 2% difference reflects physics (finite eps14 or eps12*eps34) or drift and calibration. Writing 'equal' in the abstract overstates the result, and the meaning of 'agree to about 5%' is unclear: Fig. 3b plots (f_odd - f_even)/(f_odd + f_even), and 5% in that quantity corresponds to roughly a 10% frequency ratio.
comments.suggested_fix: Replace 'equal' in the abstract with the measured relative difference (about 2%, i.e. (f_odd - f_even)/(f_odd + f_even) = 0.019), state whether '5%' in the main text refers to the normalized difference plotted in Fig. 3b, and add a systematic uncertainty estimate from repeated even/odd measurements at the same nominal tuning.

comments.title: Excited-state resonance condition is off by a factor of two
comments.quote: simplifies to −ε34 = 2|∆L |. In other words, the splitting between even and odd ground states of the
comments.explanation: With the paper's definitions, eps34 = delta_eps_R/2, where delta_eps_R = E_e - E_o (Eq. (11)). At the left-chain sweet spot with mu_L = 0, Eqs. (12)-(13) give E_eL = E_oL = -Delta_L and an even excited state at +Delta_L, so the left excitation gap is 2|Delta_L|. The condition E|oo> = E|e+ e> becomes -Delta_L + E_oR = +Delta_L + E_eR, i.e. -delta_eps_R = 2|Delta_L|, or -eps34 = |Delta_L|. The verbal statement that follows ('the splitting between even and odd ground states of the right chain must be equal to the excitation gap of the left chain') is correct and agrees with this, but the formula -eps34 = 2|Delta_L| does not, because the splitting is 2|eps34|, not |eps34|. The same factor applies to the |ee> case, written as eps34 = 2|Delta_L|. The qualitative argument about which quadrant shows the lines is unaffected, but anyone using the formula to estimate Delta_L from the position of the outer lines in Fig. 1f or Fig. ED5 would be off by a factor of two.
comments.suggested_fix: Replace −ε34 = 2|∆L| with −ε34 = |∆L| (equivalently −δϵR = 2|∆L|), and ε34 = 2|∆L| with ε34 = |∆L| (δϵR = 2|∆L|).

comments.title: Sign of the residual splitting in Methods X contradicts Eqs. (12)-(13) and the main text
comments.quote: each chain is given by δϵL/R = ∆L/R − tL/R . This difference can be changed linearly to first order with
comments.explanation: From Eqs. (12) and (13) with mu_alpha1 = mu_alpha2 = 0, E|e> = -|Delta| and E|o> = -|t|, so delta_eps = E|e> - E|o> = |t| - |Delta|. This agrees with the main text and Methods IX (eps12 = (t_L - Delta_L)/2 = delta_eps_L/2). Methods X instead writes delta_eps = Delta - t, and likewise says the critical point value vanishes for eps = |Delta_L| - |t_L|. Because the zero-splitting condition is delta_eps_L = eps, and delta_eps_L at the critical point (mu = 0) equals |t_L| - |Delta_L|, the crossing condition should be eps = |t_L| - |Delta_L|. The sign does not change the conclusion that the even and odd longitudinal terms have opposite slopes in the (V_LH, V_RH) plane. It does flip which side of the sweet spot is called CAR- or ECT-dominated when this section is combined with Eq. (11) or Fig. ED12.
comments.suggested_fix: Write δϵL/R = tL/R − ∆L/R and state the crossing condition as ϵ = |tL| − |∆L|, consistent with Eqs. (12)-(13) and ε12 = (tL − ∆L)/2.

comments.title: Frequency formula above Eq. (22) is missing a factor of 2, and its sign convention differs from Fig. 3b
comments.quote: These frequencies are feven/odd = h1 (ε23 ± ε14 )
comments.explanation: With H_even = (eps23 + eps14) X (Eq. (9) at phi = 0, Z = Y = 0), the eigenvalues are ±(eps23 + eps14), so the level splitting is 2(eps23 + eps14) and the population oscillation frequency is f = 2(eps23 + eps14)/h, not (eps23 + eps14)/h. The same convention is used correctly elsewhere: Eq. (24) gives P(t) = 1/2 + 1/2 cos(t_LR lambda t/hbar) for H = (t_LR/2) lambda Y, so f = t_LR lambda/h = 2 x (t_LR lambda/2)/h. The ratio in Eq. (22) is unaffected, but the absolute relation matters if eps23 is extracted from the measured f (e.g. t_LR ≈ h x 106 MHz ≈ 0.44 µeV). Eq. (22) also defines (f_even - f_odd)/(f_even + f_odd), while Fig. 3b plots (f_odd - f_even)/(f_odd + f_even), and the text says Eq. (22) expresses 'the frequency difference shown in Fig. 3b'. A reader converting the sign of Fig. 3b into a sign of mu_L1*mu_R2 would get the opposite sign.
comments.suggested_fix: Write f_even/odd = 2(ε23 ± ε14)/h, and either define Eq. (22) as (fodd − feven)/(fodd + feven) = −ε14/ε23 = −µL1µR2/(4tLtR) or relabel the Fig. 3b axis to match.

comments.title: Model noise parameters predict sizable dephasing at phi = pi, at odds with Fig. 2e
comments.quote: neither oscillations nor fast dephasing. This observation is consistent with the theoretical prediction that
comments.explanation:
Methods XI (Eqs. (23)-(25)) argues that at phi = pi, quasistatic noise on the outer dots produces a random transverse Y term and hence Gaussian dephasing even at the sweet spot. Using the paper's own numbers, sigma_mu = 1.5 µeV and t_L = t_R = 20 µeV (Table 1) give sigma_lambda = sqrt(2) x 1.5/40 ≈ 0.053. t_LR ≈ h x 106 MHz ≈ 0.44 µeV (consistent with t_LC*t_CR/mu_C = 7.5^2/130 ≈ 0.43 µeV). Eq. (25) then gives a 1/e time of sqrt(2) hbar/(sigma_lambda t_LR) ≈ 40 ns. This is comparable to T2Rabi = 26 ns at phi ≈ 0 and lies within the 0-40 ns window of Fig. 2e, where

would fall to about 0.68. Yet the main text says that at B_perp ≈ 11 and 16 mT there is 'neither oscillations nor fast dephasing', and Methods XI concludes that the absence of oscillations is consistent with well-decoupled Majoranas. So either the outer-dot noise is smaller than in Table 1 (and the phi ≈ 0 dephasing comes from somewhere else), or dephasing at phi = pi is present but not discussed. The account of phi = pi is also inconsistent between sections: the ED9 caption attributes the decoherence near phi = pi to 'imperfect tuning', while Methods XI says Eq. (25) 'could explain the dephasing seen in Fig. ED9b' at the sweet spot. Finally, the VC pulse amplitude used in Fig. 2e is not stated, so t_LR for that panel cannot be pinned down.
comments.suggested_fix: State the VC used in Fig. 2e, plot the measured return probability at phi ≈ pi against Eq. (25) evaluated with the Table 1 noise parameters (or the full simulation of Fig. ED10j), and reconcile the ED9 caption ('imperfect tuning') with the Methods XI explanation (noise-induced overlap at the sweet spot).

comments.title: Fixed-duration pulsed CSDs from a different cooldown are weak evidence for the phi = pi overlap argument
comments.quote: This is consistent with our experimental findings for the pulsed charge-stability diagrams at φ ≈ π
comments.explanation: Methods XI uses Fig. ED6i,j to argue that detuning the outer dot, but not the inner dot, enables a transverse coupling at phi ≈ pi, which would be direct evidence of the linear overlap term in Eq. (14). Several features of that data set weaken the inference. ED6 is taken at a single pulse duration of 10 ns, so a reduction of p(oo|ee) along a line cannot be separated into slow coherent rotation and dephasing. The text nevertheless discusses 'suppression of dephasing' and 'dephasing comparable to the case phi ≈ 0', which are time-domain statements. Methods III says the ED6/ED9 cooldown was tuned before the odd-manifold protocol existed, so the simultaneous sweet spot of both chains was not verified. The ED6 caption also notes that the right chain moves from CAR-like through the sweet spot to ECT-like as VC changes, because of uncompensated cross-capacitance. Under these conditions, asymmetry between detuning QDR1 and QDR2 could also come from the chain being off its sweet spot (t_R ≠ Delta_R), which by itself makes the two dots inequivalent.
comments.suggested_fix: Label the ED6i,j comparison as qualitative, noting that it comes from a cooldown without odd-manifold verification and at a single 10 ns duration, or replace it with time-domain single-dot detuning measurements (as in Fig. 4a-d) taken at phi ≈ pi in the main cooldown.

comments.title: The 'conventional charge qubit' comparison is not reached in the measured detuning range
comments.quote: chain (Fig. 4g,h) reduces the coupled chains to an effective double QD and provides a direct comparison
comments.explanation: The argument is that detuning one QD in each chain reduces the system to an effective double dot, and the absence of resolved oscillations shows the benefit of the poor man's Majorana encoding. Two problems remain. First, the reduction to a double QD holds only when the detuned dot's level is far from the sweet spot, |mu| >> t, Delta ≈ 20 µeV. The detuning ranges in Fig. 4g,h are about 0.6 mV, i.e. about 18 µeV with the stated lever arm alpha_i ≈ 0.03, comparable to t and Delta. The data are therefore in an intermediate regime that, according to the authors' own model, still has degenerate chain parities (Eq. (13) with one dot detuned) and only partially delocalized Majoranas. Second, panels g and h are not equivalent: in h the inner dots L2 and R1, which are adjacent to the coupler, are detuned, so the remaining resonant dots L1 and R2 are not directly tunnel-coupled to QDC and the effective 'double QD' coupling is strongly reduced. A missing oscillation there does not show that a charge qubit dephases faster. 'Under the same measurement conditions' also includes 25 ns ramps and 18-50 ns pulse windows, which could hide fast-dephasing charge oscillations of a few ns that conventional charge qubits often show.
comments.suggested_fix: Rephrase as a comparison with partially delocalized chains in the intermediate-detuning regime, quote the detuning range in energy units (about 18 µeV vs t ≈ ∆ ≈ 20 µeV), and drop the 'direct comparison to a conventional charge qubit' claim unless a deliberately prepared single-orbital double-dot configuration is measured with the same pulse protocol.

comments.title: 'First coherent control of a Majorana qubit' overstates the operations demonstrated
comments.quote: establish the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit, encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana
comments.explanation: The paper demonstrates Rabi-type oscillations about a tilted X axis, with Q = f x T2Rabi ≈ 2.8 at VC = 9.8 mV (106.7 MHz x 26 ns). The introduction states that 'arbitrary single-qubit rotations can be generated' by tuning the couplings, but no Z rotation, Ramsey sequence, echo, composite rotation or state tomography is shown, and no gate or SPAM fidelity is reported. The authors' own Methods VIII cautions that the effective Hamiltonian cannot distinguish spatially separated Majoranas from quasi-Majoranas, and that evidence for separation rests on the detuning studies, which (see other comments) are qualitative. The claim of coherent parity oscillations in a minimal Kitaev chain device is well supported. 'Coherent control of a Majorana qubit' with priority wording implies more qubit functionality, and more certainty about the Majorana character, than the data establish.
comments.suggested_fix: Rephrase the abstract and conclusion to 'coherent parity oscillations (Rabi-type rotations) of a qubit encoded in poor man's Majorana modes of two coupled minimal Kitaev chains', and either demonstrate a second rotation axis (e.g. a Ramsey sequence using a ε12 or ε34 pulse) or remove the statement that arbitrary rotations are generated in this device.

comments.title: Exponential-envelope fits are inconsistent with the quasistatic noise model, and 'close agreement' is overstated
comments.quote: Rabi oscillations were fitted to an exponentially damped cosine,
comments.explanation: The decay times T2Rabi in Fig. 2d and Fig. ED7/ED8 come from an exponential envelope, Eq. (3). The theory used to interpret them (Methods VII, XI) assumes quasistatic Gaussian noise, which gives a Gaussian envelope (as in Eq. (25)) or, for transverse-dominated noise, power-law tails, not an exponential. The numerical T2Rabi depends on the envelope chosen, and the non-monotonic T2Rabi(VC) used to argue for a crossover between coupler-noise and chain-noise regimes could shift if the envelope were changed. Methods VII also says the noise standard deviations were chosen to qualitatively reproduce the data and that 'no fitting procedure is performed', while the abstract claims oscillation frequency and coherence depend on coupling and detuning 'in close agreement with our model'. Hand-chosen noise parameters with qualitative agreement do not amount to close agreement.
comments.suggested_fix: Fit the time traces with a generalized envelope exp[-(t/T2Rabi)^n] (or directly with the quasistatic-noise model), report n, and change 'close agreement' in the abstract to 'qualitative agreement'.

comments.title: Fit range for Rabi frequencies is inconsistent with the stated resolvable range
comments.quote: In Fig. 2 and Fig. 3, only data with VC < 11.25 mV were included in this fit, as the
comments.explanation: The main text says the oscillations become too fast to resolve near 11.2 mV, and the inverse-detuning fit in Fig. ED7m uses VC < 10.8 mV. With the fitted K = 156.6 MHz·mV and V0 = 11.285 mV, the expected frequency at VC = 11.2 mV is about 1.8 GHz and at 11.25 mV about 4.5 GHz. That is far above anything that can be sampled with a 2 ns native grid and 25 ns ramps, and above the 600 MHz range shown in Fig. 2c. Including 10.8 < VC < 11.25 mV in the damped-cosine fits would either give aliased frequencies or fits that fail. Three different cutoffs (11.2, 11.25, 10.8 mV) appear without explanation. The fitted V0 = 11.285 mV is also slightly below the ≈11.5 mV resonance roughly identified in Fig. ED2e. This may reflect different configurations, but it is worth reconciling since V0 sets the detuning axis of Fig. ED7m.
comments.suggested_fix: State one cutoff consistently (e.g. VC < 10.8 mV, where predicted f < 330 MHz), give the maximum frequency that can be resolved with the sub-grid pulse-duration scheme, and comment on the difference between V0 = 11.285 mV and the resonance estimate from Fig. ED2e.

comments.title: Simulated pulse protocol (sudden quench) differs from the experimental 25 ns ramps
comments.quote: We consider the initial state |ψ0 ⟩ = |ee⟩ where two chains are
comments.explanation: The simulation starts from |ee> at mu_C → infinity and evolves under the coupled Hamiltonian for a square pulse of duration T, i.e. an instantaneous change of mu_C. In the experiment, the chain QDs and coupler are ramped over 25 ns, and Fig. ED2b explicitly shows that the qubit evolves during the ramp (oscillations versus ramp time at zero pulse duration). Fig. ED2e also shows that fast ramps (≲5 ns) cause diabatic excitation of the chain-coupler system. A sudden quench therefore does not describe the experimental state preparation, and it affects the zero-time phase, the apparent contrast, and possibly the detuning dependence in Figs. ED10 and ED11 that are compared with Figs. ED7 and ED8. For the parameters in Table 1 the quench admixture is small (about (t_LC/mu_C)^2 ≈ 0.3%), so the main effect is the missing ramp evolution, not leakage. It still means the simulated 'pulse duration' is not the same quantity as the experimental one.
comments.suggested_fix: Include the 25 ns linear ramps of µC and of the chain chemical potentials in the time-dependent simulation (U = T exp(−i∫H(t)dt/ℏ)), or state explicitly that the simulated duration corresponds to the plateau only and that the ramp evolution is neglected.

comments.title: Phase calibration after the half-period phase jump is unclear in the main text
comments.quote: jump, an out-of-plane magnetic field of 15.6 mT corresponded to φ ≈ 0. After the jump, the magnetic-
comments.explanation: Most data are taken at B_perp = 15.6 mT, identified as phi ≈ 0 from Fig. ED7o. Fig. 2e was taken after a phase jump of about 2.5 mT, which is half the 5 mT period, so it amounts to a shift of phi by about pi. In Fig. 2e the frequency is suppressed near 16 mT, i.e. close to the field value used as phi ≈ 0 for the other main-text data. The main text says only that measurements are at phi ≈ 0 unless stated otherwise and does not mention the jump, so a reader comparing Fig. 2e with the ED7 caption could conclude that the main data were taken near phi ≈ pi. Since the phi ≈ 0 assignment for Figs. 2a, 3 and 4 rests on ED7o, which was acquired after those data (Methods III acquisition order), it is also worth stating what evidence shows that no jump occurred during those earlier measurements.
comments.suggested_fix: Add to the Fig. 2e caption that this data set was acquired after a phase jump of about 2.5 mT (≈ π), so that φ ≈ π occurs near 11 and 16 mT here while 15.6 mT corresponds to φ ≈ 0 for the other main-text data, and state how the absence of earlier jumps was checked.

comments.title: Readout and parity-switch mapping fidelities are not reported, though contrast is used as a tuning criterion
comments.quote: For operations in the odd manifold, we use the parity-switching dot to
comments.explanation: All conditional probabilities are raw single-shot assignments, and the leakage floor of about 5% in Fig. 2b is attributed to readout error. No assignment fidelities for |ee>, |oo> and the odd states are given, beyond Gaussian-mixture thresholds and dwell times. In the odd manifold, every data point also relies on two passes of the QDPS pulse (in and out), applied through a DC line with RC filtering, and the fidelity of that mapping is not quantified. A failed in-mapping leaves the system in the even manifold evolving under H_even, which then reads out as leakage or, if both mappings fail, as even-manifold dynamics recorded as odd. This matters because Methods III uses 'similar frequencies and contrast in both manifolds' as the success criterion, and Fig. 3d-j compares contrast between manifolds. Without the mapping fidelity, a lower or different contrast in the odd manifold cannot be interpreted physically.
comments.suggested_fix: Report single-shot assignment fidelities for |ee>, |oo> and the odd sector in the readout configuration of Fig. ED3e-g, and the QDPS mapping fidelity measured by applying the QDPS pulse twice with no chain pulse (ideal outcome p(ee|ee) = 1), so that contrasts in the two manifolds can be compared on equal footing.
